rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with `name:` front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`.

The requirement lets a skill put specialized material in linked files. It requires each such link to say when to read the file.

The skill has no Markdown links. It points to three `references/` files only as inline code, and each pointer says when to read the file:
- `references/authoring-failures.md` (habeas-evidence skill): step 1 says "If it fails, read…", right after the `habeas author --stdout <full-name>` check.
- `references/distributed-requirements.md` (habeas skill): "When a convention applies on its own at many sites… read…".
- `references/fixme.md` (habeas-evidence skill): given for the case where the user defers a possible-bug requirement, which gets a `{fixme}` reference.

These files belong to other skills, so the obligation may not strictly cover them. Even if it does, each pointer states its trigger, so I found no gap. The site has no violation matches to judge.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
